messages:
maria: quick sync — planning to roll out a lightweight canary telemetry adaptor for runtime inputs. goal: give product + SRE a single dashboard that compares candidate vs baseline across latency, cost, and signal regressions. putting this here so infra/runtime/devex can weigh in :wave:
kevin: SG — do we have a concrete set of metrics to start with or are we still brainstorming?
sanjay: need to be careful about cardinality. per-route + per-model-variant is useful but we should avoid exploding label combos. maybe stick to route + variant + env (canary/control) to start.
liz: dashboard UX ask: top row should be paired p50/p95 latencies, then a delta column that shows relative change with sparklines. also a widget for 'regression_score' so PMs can quickly triage.
matt: sampling / cost question — ingesting per-request traces for every canary will be expensive. propose we compute aggregates at runtime and emit minute buckets, not per-request.
maria: agreed on minute-buckets. we also need kv-cache-hit-rate, batch_efficiency (tokens per batch), model-fallback-count, quota_throttle_count. these are the runtime inputs we can surface.
priya: for rollouts UX, we should let users click a diff and see example traces / prompts that caused the regression. that requires keeping a small sample of full requests tied to the time window. can we store 100 samples per route per hour?
sanjay: 100 samples/hr per route might still be a lot. can we keep sampled_request_ids and fetch payloads on demand from S3 with an ACL? reduces streaming cost.
kevin: on tag consistency: we need a contract for labels. draft proposal: {route, env, model_variant, model_version, cluster_region}. everything else goes into freeform attrs.
maria: sounds good. also adding a boolean label `canary=true` for routing.
metrics-bot: Note — new metric schema PR opened: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/482 (assigned to @sanjay) :robot_face:
sanjay: PR has proto sketch. question for infra: do we want sum vs gauge for batch_efficiency? it's an average computed over tokens/batch, so gauge seems fine.
matt: agree gauge. for cache-hit-rate use 'ratio' with numerator/denom to allow precise alerting.
liz: for the dashboard, can we surface a computed column 'cost_delta' that multiplies tokens * unit_token_cost per route? product wants quick signal of cost regressions.
kevin: need to confirm unit_token_cost source — is that billing or estimate from runtime config? should be consistent across routes.
maria: runtime will expose `estimated_token_cost_per_minute` metric so the dashboard can compute cost_delta client-side if needed.
priya: rollout controls: add a gating rule in console: if regression_score > 0.12 OR p95_delta > 20% for 10m => auto-pause canary. we should prototype with a lower threshold.
sanjay: telemetry ingestion note: attach trace_id and sample_reason to sampled items so we can pull traces.
matt: ops concern — tagging must be stable across deploys. model_version label should be semver-ish or commit hash, but UI needs human-friendly alias.
liz: UI will show alias + tooltip with model_version. also include 'why' link that opens the sample set used for scoring.
maria: next steps: sanjay to update proto with labels & bucket frequency, matt to run cost calc on sample workload, liz/priya to draft dashboard wireframe and gating UX, kevin to own the ingestion SLOs. sync tomorrow 10am.
kevin: ack. I'll also add a small log line to runtime that emits the metric counts at minute boundary:
```
# runtime snippet (pseudo)
emit_metric("runtime.batch_efficiency", value=avg_tokens_per_batch, labels={route, model_variant, env, canary})
emit_metric("runtime.kv_cache_hit", numerator=hits, denom=reqs, labels={route, env})
```
maria: thanks everyone — trying to keep this minimal for first rollout. if we hit blind spots we'll iterate. :+1:
